diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS), non-germinal-center B-cell-like (non-GCB/ABC-like) by the Hans algorithm (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 positive), with a double-expressor immunophenotype (MYC about 45%, BCL2 about 70%) but no MYC, BCL2, or BCL6 rearrangement on FISH, so it is not a double-hit/triple-hit high-grade B-cell lymphoma. Ki-67 about 80%, EBER negative, CD5 negative. Metastatic breast carcinoma is excluded by morphology and by negative cytokeratin AE1/AE3 and GATA3 in the lesional cells. Ann Arbor/Lugano stage III with splenic involvement (IIIS); IPI 2.
stage: Ann Arbor/Lugano stage III S: supradiaphragmatic left axillary and mediastinal (prevascular/left paratracheal) nodal disease, plus infradiaphragmatic mesenteric and para-aortic nodal disease and multiple FDG-avid splenic nodules. Bone marrow is negative and there is no non-lymphatic extranodal organ involvement (no liver, lung, bone, adrenal, kidney, or CNS disease), so this is stage III rather than IV. The largest mass is the 7.5 cm mesenteric conglomerate; it does not meet the NCCN >=10 cm definition of bulky disease. IPI 2 (stage III and elevated LDH; age 59, ECOG 1, no more than one extranodal site). CNS-IPI 2 (intermediate CNS risk, but no high-risk anatomic site).
biology: Non-GCB/ABC-like DLBCL by Hans (CD10 negative, BCL6 positive, MUM1 positive in about 80%), with high proliferation (Ki-67 about 80%), BCL2 about 70% and MYC about 45% by IHC, meeting criteria for double-expressor lymphoma (MYC >=40%, BCL2 >=50%). FISH is negative for MYC (8q24), BCL2 (18q21), and BCL6 (3q27) rearrangements, so this is not double-hit/triple-hit and not a high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC/BCL2 rearrangement. EBER is negative, CD5 is negative, and cyclin D1 is negative. The non-GCB/ABC and double-expressor phenotype is associated with inferior response to R-CHOP and is the rationale for considering Pola-R-CHP or novel agents, but the cardiac comorbidity constrains anthracycline use. No TP53 sequencing or gene-expression profiling is available.
prognosis: Potentially curable with anthracycline-based immunochemotherapy, but the double-expressor/non-GCB biology and high Ki-67 place her at above-average risk of primary refractory or relapsed disease. IPI 2 is low-intermediate (original IPI 5-year OS about 50-60% in the CHOP era, better with rituximab), R-IPI 2 is 'good' (4-year PFS about 80%), and NCCN-IPI 2 is low-intermediate. I would quote a cure probability of roughly 60% (range about 50-70%), with the caveat that cardiac comorbidity may limit full-dose anthracycline delivery. Response to treatment is the strongest prognostic factor; a Deauville 4-5 end-of-treatment PET or primary progression would substantially worsen prognosis and prompt salvage/CAR-T planning.
first_line_treatment: Curative intent: R-CHOP x6 cycles every 21 days (rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV day 1; cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV day 1; doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 IV day 1; vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 IV day 1, capped at 2 mg; prednisone 100 mg PO days 1-5). Because she has already received 240 mg/m2 doxorubicin and has an LVEF of 45% with GLS -14%, I would give dexrazoxane cardioprotection with each doxorubicin dose per label and co-manage with cardio-oncology. If cardio-oncology judges that any further anthracycline is unacceptable, or if LVEF falls further or she develops heart failure, I would switch to R-CEOP x6 (etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1-3 replacing doxorubicin). I would not use Pola-R-CHP because it still contains doxorubicin and she has an LVEF of 45%; the pivotal POLARIX trial enrolled patients with preserved cardiac function, and this regimen would not address her main toxicity concern. No consolidation radiotherapy and no CNS-directed prophylaxis. Continue anastrozole to complete 10 years in November 2026; there is no clinically significant interaction with R-CHOP.
cns_risk: CNS-IPI 2 (stage III and elevated LDH; age <60, ECOG 1, no more than one extranodal site, no kidney/adrenal involvement) = intermediate risk, approximately 4% 2-year risk (CNS-IPI low 0-1, intermediate 2-3, high 4-6). There is no testicular, breast, adrenal, kidney, epidural, or bone marrow involvement, and no CNS symptoms. I would not give intrathecal methotrexate or high-dose methotrexate and would not perform a diagnostic lumbar puncture. I would reassess if she develops neurologic symptoms, if the pathology is revised to a double-hit/high-grade lymphoma, or if a high-risk site (for example testis, breast, adrenal, kidney, or epidural) is found.
response_assessment: Use Lugano 2014 criteria with FDG-PET/CT because the baseline disease is FDG-avid. I would not routinely do an interim PET after 2 cycles; if one is obtained, Deauville 1-3 does not alter the plan and Deauville 4-5 must be confirmed by biopsy because of false positives with rituximab. The key assessment is end-of-treatment FDG-PET/CT about 6-8 weeks (up to 12 weeks) after cycle 6: Deauville 1-3 = complete metabolic response; Deauville 4-5 = residual uptake requiring biopsy. Bone marrow was negative at baseline, so it does not need to be repeated. If end-of-treatment PET shows persistent disease, proceed to platinum-based salvage with or without rituximab and evaluate for CAR-T (axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, or tisagenlecleucel) or autologous transplant. Reassess LVEF by echocardiogram before, during (after 2-3 cycles), and after therapy. If complete response, surveillance with history/exam and imaging only for symptoms; no consolidation radiation.
pretreatment_workup: Already completed and adequate: excisional left axillary node biopsy with IHC and FISH; whole-body FDG PET-CT; bone marrow aspirate/biopsy (negative); CBC with differential, CMP, LDH, uric acid, beta-2 microglobulin, creatinine/eGFR; HIV, hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc, anti-HBs), and hepatitis C serologies; transthoracic echocardiogram; and ECOG performance status. Before starting therapy I would add: cardio-oncology consultation with baseline troponin/NT-proBNP and consideration of cardiac MRI if the echo is equivocal; obtain the prior breast radiotherapy records and estimate cardiac dose; optimize heart-failure therapy (ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker) and blood pressure; dental evaluation; document vaccination status and give inactivated influenza/pneumococcal/COVID vaccines before rituximab (live vaccines are contraindicated during and for at least 6 months after rituximab); baseline TSH, lipid panel, and HbA1c as part of cardiac risk assessment; and a hematopathology second review if there is any diagnostic uncertainty. Lumbar puncture and CNS imaging are not indicated. Pregnancy testing is not needed.
supportive_care: Cardio-oncology: baseline and serial echocardiograms, troponin/NT-proBNP, guideline-directed heart-failure therapy (ACE inhibitor/ARB plus beta-blocker) and BP control, dexrazoxane with each doxorubicin dose, and careful fluid balance because of LVEF 45%. Antiemetics: 5-HT3 antagonist plus dexamethasone, with an NK1 antagonist and/or olanzapine for breakthrough; dexamethasone exposure is already part of R-CHOP. Primary G-CSF prophylaxis with pegfilgrastim 6 mg SC on day 2 (or equivalent filgrastim) because of the myelosuppressive regimen and her age/comorbidity; teach febrile-neutropenia precautions. Tumor lysis prophylaxis: allopurinol 300 mg daily (renal function is normal) with hydration and frequent uric acid/electrolyte/creatinine monitoring for at least the first cycle; rasburicase if uric acid rises or TLS develops, given the bulky mesenteric mass and high LDH. Infection: no routine PJP or antiviral prophylaxis for R-CHOP; consider TMP-SMX if prolonged corticosteroids are used; HBV antiviral prophylaxis is not needed because HBsAg and anti-HBc are negative, but she is anti-HBs negative and should be vaccinated when appropriate. VTE prophylaxis is not routine (Khorana score 1), but use LMWH if hospitalized or if additional risk. Constipation prophylaxis with vincristine (senna/laxatives), monitor for neuropathy. Steroid precautions: glucose and BP monitoring, sleep/mood support, bone protection with calcium/vitamin D. Continue anastrozole; maintain weight-bearing exercise and a healthy diet; psychosocial support and work accommodations; discuss hair loss; fertility is not relevant.
fitness_and_goals: She is fit for curative-intent full-dose immunochemotherapy: 59 years old, ECOG 1, independent, working full time, no frailty, normal renal and hepatic function, and a supportive husband who drives her to visits. Her goals are cure and return to full-time work, which aligns with aggressive first-line therapy. The main vulnerability is cardiac: LVEF 45% (down from 62%), GLS -14%, prior doxorubicin 240 mg/m2, left breast radiotherapy, hypertension, and a family history of heart failure. I would explicitly discuss that the cardiac finding changes the regimen: R-CHOP will be given only with dexrazoxane cardioprotection, and R-CEOP is reserved for the situation where further anthracycline is judged unsafe. Cure remains the priority and can still be pursued. Shared decision-making should include the trade-off between the proven R-CHOP backbone and the less cardiotoxic but less well-studied R-CEOP, as well as the small risk of secondary malignancy and the planned completion of anastrozole. If she develops symptomatic heart failure or LVEF falls, the plan shifts to non-anthracycline therapy; if she remains fit and cardiac function is stable, complete 6 cycles and assess response. Code status and advance care planning are not documented but can be addressed later.
missing_information: Explicit Lugano/Ann Arbor stage documentation in a staged Condition resource (I derived stage III S from the PET/CT and bone marrow).
Cardio-oncology assessment and baseline cardiac biomarkers (troponin, NT-proBNP), plus consideration of cardiac MRI, given LVEF 45% and GLS -14%.
Prior left breast radiotherapy records with an estimate of cardiac radiation dose, and confirmation of the cumulative anthracycline dose (240 mg/m2 is documented).
Current cardiac medications and whether an ACE inhibitor/ARB and beta-blocker are tolerated; only amlodipine is listed.
Vaccination status (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19) and any prior live-vaccine exposure.
Hepatitis B vaccination status and any need for HBV DNA monitoring, since anti-HBs is nonreactive (HBsAg and anti-HBc are negative).
Baseline TSH, lipid panel, and HbA1c for cardiac risk assessment.
Patient preferences about alopecia, work schedule, and quality-of-life trade-offs, and insurance coverage for dexrazoxane or alternative regimens.
Whether anastrozole will be continued during chemotherapy (I recommend continuing; no significant interaction is documented).
Code status and advance care planning, and any distress/quality-of-life screening.
Expert hematopathology second opinion, TP53 sequencing, or gene-expression profiling (not standard, but would refine the double-expressor/non-GCB biology).
